# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "sphms",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "sphms-theory.html",
    Implementation = "sphms-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "sphms-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "sphms-validation.html"
  )
)
```

SPHMS is benchmarked against the spherical Jech et al. reference definitions stored in `benchmark_ts` [@Jech_2015]. The comparison is intentionally simple: the same spherical geometry and boundary condition are evaluated in acousticTS, then compared to the stored target-strength curve in dB.

::: {.tip data-title="Read benchmark deltas in context"}
Small dB residuals are most meaningful when the benchmark and reproduced case share the same radius, medium properties, boundary condition, frequency grid, and reporting quantity.
:::

## Benchmark summary

| Boundary | Max abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Elapsed (s) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `fixed_rigid` | 0.00497 | 0.00246 | 0.03 |
| `pressure_release` | 0.00500 | 0.00243 | 0.09 |
| `gas_filled` | 0.00499 | 0.00263 | 0.06 |
| `liquid_filled` | 0.00492 | 0.00241 | 0.11 |

All four spherical boundary types stay within about `0.005 dB` of the stored benchmark family across the tested grid.

## Modal-limit sensitivity

SPHMS exposes `m_limit`, so the benchmark suite also checks how much the liquid-filled result moves when the modal cap is reduced.

| Boundary | `m_limit` | Max abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Mean abs. $\Delta$ TS (dB) | Elapsed (s) |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `liquid_filled` | default rule | 0.00492 | 0.00241 | 0.07 |
| `liquid_filled` | `20` | 0.52550 | 0.00640 | 0.14 |
| `liquid_filled` | `10` | 58.24225 | 8.07819 | 0.02 |

Aggressive under-truncation can reduce elapsed time, but it can also destroy the benchmark fit. In normal use, `m_limit` should be treated as a convergence-control override rather than a tuning parameter.
